rationale: The successor experiment executed in a clean copy (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f, completed, exit 0) and reproduced the witness with every comparison complete and evaluated: the re-added voter's invocation did not return within the window, released only on the caller's own deadline, and its payload was never committed, while the never-removed member and the same node after a leader change returned immediately and committed. This update attributes that retained interpretation, adds the snapshot's own node-level expectation about when proposal blocking is intended as a source anchor, and records the resulting knowledge. No new experiment is submitted: the open discriminator is answered and an unchanged repeat would add no evidence.

knowledge.statement: The captured node-level test defines the intended proposal-blocking condition as 'does not know who is the current leader': it asserts that a Propose invocation on a node without a leader does not return, and then asserts that after the node campaigns and installs a leader the same pending invocation returns NoError. The test therefore scopes intended blocking to the unknown-leader case and expects acceptance once a leader is known; it exercises no removal/re-addition path and does not cover a member that is re-added while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter test node driven through the async Node API (newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1)), newNode + go n.run()); the assertion is on the invocation issued before any leader is known, and on the same invocation once the node becomes leader.

interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts come from the same fixed scenario lineage: 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment was registered as the successor (previous_id 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment) of the experiment executed as 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad, and its only input difference is the event naming in the harness (distinct per-operation names instead of shared propose_result/propose_invocation/commit_observation names), recorded in its revision_reason. Both runs build the same three-node configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, apply the same committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes on node 3, use identical operation ids, payloads, phases, deadlines and windows (witness deadline 2500 ms, window 1200 ms; control deadline 5000 ms; repair window 2000 ms), and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2. The receipts therefore describe the same identities and events, with decisive fields agreeing index for index (witness 7/8/9, control 11/12, repair 15/16); only the successor additionally carries the witness_release comparison.
interpretations.rationale: Two retained executions of the same fixed scenario agree. In a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f (successor harness, distinct per-operation event names) all seven comparisons are complete and evaluated as holds: the re-admission of node 3 was applied on node 3 (index 4: change add, ok true, voter true, leader 1, term 1), the node context recorded node 3 as a voter with leader 1 (index 5), the invocation was admitted (index 6: phase after_readmission, leader 1, deadline 2500 ms), it had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7: returned false, err empty, elapsed_ms 1200), it released only when the caller's deadline expired (index 8: err 'context deadline exceeded', elapsed_ms 2501), and its payload appeared in no node's committed entries (index 9: present false, observed_nodes null). The control on never-removed node 2 with the same leader 1 returned in 0 ms (index 11) and was committed on all three nodes (index 12); after the forced campaign produced leader 2 at term 2 (index 13) the same node 3 invocation returned in 0 ms (index 15) and was committed on all three nodes (index 16). The earlier receipt 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad shows the identical values at the corresponding indices (witness 7/8/9, control 11/12, repair 15/16), so the difference is a property of the scenario, not of one run. The source account identifies the mechanism: the run loop's proposal gate is assigned only at node.go:374, 377 and 426 and read for proposals at node.go:525; re-admission cannot enter the removal guard (node.go:401-412) because the local Progress entry is already gone, so MsgProp is offered to a nil channel and can end only via the caller's context or node stop. The snapshot's own node test (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader and expects the invocation to be accepted once a leader is known, which is precisely the condition the re-added voter satisfies while still being blocked; no test in the snapshot removes and re-adds a member through the Node API. The control also excludes the rival explanations that the cluster or leader was stalled (index 12) or that node 3's own state machine could not forward proposals (index 16).
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the leader-change dependence but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended behavior for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case (a voter with a known leader), and the same test asserts that the invocation is accepted once a leader is known.

The witnessed interval is bounded by the caller's context (index 8), so the claim is a bounded non-completion under a stable leader rather than an unbounded deadlock; the proposal is neither delivered nor rejected within that interval.
limitations: Framework comparison outcomes for the first receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names, so each comparison also evaluated the other operations' events; the first receipt's decisive events are still complete and match the successor's ones, and the successor receipt has complete holds for all seven comparisons.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose has no such gate. No tick was delivered and delivery was reliable, so no network-fault or timing characterization is claimed.

Only the voter-removal form was executed. Other authority transitions that delete the local Progress entry (for example a joint change that removes the node while leaving it out of both halves) are variants of the same cause and were not executed separately.
Whether a caller with an unbounded context is released at all is not observed; the experiment used bounded contexts so the invocation interval is measured rather than assumed.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
MsgProp on a nil propc blocks until context expiry or node stop
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
